notes.body: He opens on his clothes and never strays far from them: patchwork fabric, old pieces worn with pride, and water everywhere. The water lines are an early sign of the Wavy persona that runs through everything he makes after this.

notes.title: Nile River
notes.body: The longest river in Africa, and the setup for the old pun on denial. It also keeps the water imagery going.

notes.title: Nival
notes.body: A rare word for anything to do with snow. He uses it to say his outfit keeps him ice cold.

notes.title: Jodeci
notes.body: The North Carolina R&B group of K-Ci, JoJo, DeVante Swing and Mr. Dalvin, behind 90s slow jams like Forever My Lady and Come and Talk to Me. It's what he puts on as the night winds down.

notes.title: Soul for Real
notes.body: An R&B group of four brothers from Long Island whose first single went top five in 1995. He names the group and that hit in the same line.

notes.title: Pharrell Williams
notes.body: The Virginia producer and singer who sang lead on Daft Punk's 2013 hit. The line borrows that song's title and points it at someone else.

notes.title: Chucky
notes.body: The killer doll from the Child's Play horror films. The insult is built out of the series' title.

notes.title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
notes.body: The late 90s TV series about a teenage girl who hunts vampires. Someone who hides from daylight belongs in her world.

notes.title: Doja Cat
notes.body: Her breakout single was climbing the charts in early 2020, the same season this song came out. He tucks her name and that song's title into one line.
The beat drops back for a spoken passage aimed at a woman across the room. It comes straight out of the 90s R&B slow jams he names earlier in the song, the smooth talk between verses.

notes.title: Amelia Earhart
notes.body: The aviation pioneer who disappeared over the Pacific in 1937. Fly means stylish here and also points to flight, the imagery Jett2Fly's name brings into the music.

notes.title: SWV
notes.body: Sisters With Voices, the New York trio behind some of the biggest R&B hits of 1993. He works two of their best known songs into back-to-back lines.
The last line credits the song to the two of them as a team. Jett2Fly and SyWavy make nearly everything themselves, and this early single says so on the record.
